title: Forces and Movement
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Forces and Movement Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_code: Grade 4, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Forces (pushes and pulls) change the motion and shape of objects; friction slows moving objects; gravity pulls objects toward the Earth. Learners observe, measure and predict the effects of forces. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 4, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy): pushes and pulls, friction, gravity, patterns of motion and force investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A force is a push or a pull.
key_sub: Friction slows things down; gravity pulls things toward Earth.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull. Forces can start, stop, speed up, slow down or turn an object.

  • Contact forces happen when objects touch, like friction and pushes.
  • Non-contact forces act from a distance, like gravity and magnetism.
  • Smooth surfaces like ice have little friction; rough surfaces like carpet have more.
Example

Which force pulls a ball down a slide?

It always pulls down.

Answer: gravity

Example

Why does a rolling ball stop on grass?

Rubbing surfaces

Answer: friction slows it down

Common mistakes

  • Thinking moving objects stop because they 'run out of force'.
  • Thinking gravity only acts on heavy objects.
  • Thinking friction is always bad.
